lines.trans: Max treated me very badly.
Stop crying, Nastya, wipe your tears.
You just need to get back at him.
Will I feel better if I get revenge?
Of course, you will immediately feel better.
But how can I punish him?
Start going out with his best friend.
With his friend? With bartender Kostya?
Yes, exactly with Kostya!
That way Max will hurt even more.
Do you think that's really a good idea?
Trust me, this is the very best option.
Act right now, do not lose time.
You just need to get back at him.
Start going out with his best friend.
That way Max will hurt even more.
Trust me, this is the very best option.

Stop crying, Nastya, wipe your tears.
You just need to get back at him.
Will I feel better if I get revenge?
Of course, you will immediately feel better.
But how can I punish him?
Start going out with his best friend.
With his friend? With bartender Kostya?
Yes, exactly with Kostya!
That way Max will hurt even more.
Do you think that's really a good idea?
Trust me, this is the very best option.
Act right now, do not lose time.
I will prove that I am strong.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'bartender', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Бармен наливает холодную воду в стакан.
examples.trans: The bartender pours cold water into the glass.

examples.text: Бармен, принесите нам бокал белого вина!
examples.trans: Bartender, bring us a glass of white wine!

meanings.note: impersonal: мне больно = it hurts (me)
Secondary conversational sense ('painfully') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: других вариантов нет = there are no other options

examples.text: Пробуем, других вариантов у нас нет.
examples.trans: Let's try it, we have no other options.

examples.text: Это самый лучший вариант для всех.
examples.trans: This is the very best option for everyone.

examples.text: Трава, говорите? Отлично! Пробуем, других вариантов у нас нет.
examples.trans: Herbs, you say? Excellent! Let's try it, we have no other options.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'time', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

встречаться.gloss: to meet; to date, to go out

meanings.en: to date, to go out (with someone)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'тречаться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to meet', forming an aspectual pair with 'встретиться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.
Secondary conversational sense ('to meet up') (+ с + instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We've been dating for a month.
We've been going out for a month already.

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'тереть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to wipe', forming an aspectual pair with 'вытирать'.

examples.text: Когда не можешь сам себе нос вытереть.
examples.trans: When you can't even wipe your own nose yourself.
Wipe your hands with a towel.

examples.text: Я уже вытерла слёзы и готова.
examples.trans: I already dried my tears and am ready.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Настроение у меня действительно очень хорошее.
examples.trans: My mood really is very good.
This is indeed an important question.

действовать.gloss: to act, to take action; to work

meanings.en: to act, to take action, to get to work
meanings.note: правило действует = the rule is in force

meanings.en: to work, to be in effect
meanings.note: правило действует = the rule is in force

examples.trans: Come on, Danya, go. Get to work!

meanings.note: что и требовалось доказать = Q.E.D., which is what needed to be proved

examples.trans: There, which is what needed to be proved!

examples.text: Я обязательно докажу своё кулинарное мастерство.
examples.trans: I will definitely prove my culinary mastery.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Secondary conversational sense ('still, yet') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('even (with comparatives)') (ещё больше = even more) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'idea' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Хорошая идея! Я сейчас же попробую.
examples.trans: Good idea! I will try right now.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right
Secondary conversational sense ('namely') (а именно = namely) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.
Secondary conversational sense ('as') (как вы знаете = as you know) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'of course'.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'easily'.

examples.trans: It's easy for you to say.

examples.text: Да это легко. Схватил собачку в парке и побежал.
examples.trans: Come on, it's easy. Grab the little dog in the park and run.

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world
Secondary conversational sense ('better') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'can', forming an aspectual pair with 'смочь'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'казать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to punish', forming an aspectual pair with 'наказывать'.
+ imperfective infinitive or + accusative

examples.text: Это хорошо, что готово. А то мы уже начали беспокоиться.
examples.trans: It's good that it's ready. We were starting to worry.

examples.text: Ну что, коллеги, давайте начнём наше утреннее совещание!
examples.trans: Well then, colleagues, let us begin our morning meeting!

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

отомстить.gloss: to take revenge, to get back at

meanings.en: to take revenge, to avenge oneself
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'омстить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to take revenge', forming an aspectual pair with 'мстить'.

examples.trans: He wants to get back at his neighbour.

examples.text: Эдик, я хотела тебе изменить. С ним, чтобы отомстить.
examples.trans: Edik, I wanted to cheat on you. With him, to take revenge.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cry, to weep', paired with 'заплакать'.

examples.trans: Why is the little girl crying?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'badly'.
Secondary conversational sense ('it's bad') (predicative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: + dative of the person: поверить ему

examples.text: Со своего телефона? И все поверили?
examples.trans: From your own phone? And everyone believed it?

поступить.gloss: to enter, to get into (a university); to act

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ступить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to enter', forming an aspectual pair with 'поступать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to act, to behave') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Yulia needs to get into university.

examples.text: Вы плохо поступили, но хотя бы совесть есть.
examples.trans: You acted badly, but at least you have a conscience.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'straight'.
Secondary conversational sense ('straight ahead') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Secondary conversational sense ('the very') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.en: strong, powerful (also used as a noun: the strong)
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ильный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strong, powerful').

examples.text: Сильный ищет способ, а слабый ищет причину.
examples.trans: The strong man looks for a way, and the weak man looks for an excuse.
A strong wind was blowing outside.

examples.text: Надо заманить его на свою территорию. Там, где ты сильный.
examples.trans: You need to lure him onto your territory. Right where you are strong.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'tear', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: She ran past all in tears?
She could barely hold back her tears.

examples.text: Пробежала вся в слезах? А куда она могла пойти?
examples.trans: She ran past all in tears? And where could she have gone?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'разу').

examples.trans: You can see it at once.
Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: + instrumental: стал сентиментальным
Secondary conversational sense ('to start (doing)') (+ infinitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты слишком сентиментальным стал. А лидер должен быть жёстким.
examples.trans: You've become too sentimental. And a leader has to be tough.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('so') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('like that, so') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to lose', forming an aspectual pair with 'потерять'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to waste (time)') (терять время) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Вы зря теряете время. Шпионить для вас я не буду.
examples.trans: You're wasting your time. I'm not going to spy for you.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: impersonal, + genitive: денег не хватило = there wasn't enough money
Secondary conversational sense ('that's enough!') (хватит!) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Gum? I didn't have enough money.

examples.text: Хватит спорить из-за пустяков, давайте лучше спокойно работать!
examples.trans: Enough arguing over trifles, let us just work calmly instead!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('what') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('that') (conjunction) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = well?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
